grades.quote: Xv6 performs a few: mapping the same memory (a trampoline page) in several address spaces, guarding kernel and user stacks with an unmapped page, and allocating user heap memory lazily.
grades.reason: Provides background on sharing trampoline memory across address spaces, but not why its virtual address must remain identical.

grades.quote: The trampoline page mapping at the same virtual address in user and kernel page tables allows userret to keep executing after changing satp.
grades.reason: Directly explains that identical virtual addresses allow execution to continue after switching page tables.
